newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close firmer on BNI, blue-chips.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close firmer on BNI, blue-chips.

text.p: Jakarta shares closed higher in active trading on Thursday on the back of strong buying interest in Bank Negara Indonesia and a few blue-chips, brokers said.
Trading in Bank Negara Indonesia dominated the market with 70.4 million shares changing hands on the regular board. It rose 125 rupiah -- 9.26 percent -- to 1,425 rupiah.
The bank was also active on the cross-board, trading at 1,400 rupiah on a volume of 9.7 million shares.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 2.63 points, or 0.40 percent, to close at 658.70 points, after touching a low of 655.60 points.
Gainers led losers by 71 to 47, with 61 counters unchanged. Total volume was 261.9 million shares on a turnover of 500.82 billion rupiah.
Brokers said Bank Negara Indonesia was boosted by intense market talk that the firm would be included in the Morgan Stanley Composite Index and predictions of better-than-expected 1996 earnings.
"The rise was mostly due to market rumours that, starting February 15, Morgan Stanley will include Bank Negara Indonesia in its index," a broker with a Singapore brokerage firm said.
An investor relations official with Bank Negara declined to comment on the MSCI rumours.
But he said the bank would announce its 1996 results in the second week of February.
Mirza Adityaswara, analyst at BZW Niaga Securities, said he expected the bank would book 1996 earnings in a range of 330 to 335 billion rupiah.

"This is slightly higher than the company's forecast of 326 or 327 billion rupiah it predicted at a meeting with analysts before the initial public offering last year," he said. It was listed on the Jakarta exchange on November 25.
Blue-chips such as Indosat, Astra International, Sampoerna and medium-sized issues including Indah Kiat and Bakrie Brothers were among targets for both local and foreign buyers, brokers said.

Satellite and international telephone operator Indosat was up 150 rupiah at 6,975 rupiah on a volume of 3.3 million shares after touching 7,025 rupiah. Brokers said was linked to news of a submarine cable deal signed on Wednesday in Singapore.

New York-listed shares of Indosat closed 5/8 higher at $29 overnight. Indosat said on Thursday it expected the $1.3 billion submarine cable deal to help service its estimated 15 percent average annual traffic growth. "The submarine project will help Indosat meet growing demand," investor relations manager Budi Prasetyo told Reuters.
On Wednesday, some 90 firms including Indosat signed a deal in Singapore to build a 38,000 km network linking the South Pacific to the North Atlantic across Asia and the Middle East.
The network is scheduled to open for commercial traffic by the end of 1998.
Cigarette maker Sampoerna rose 400 rupiah to 13,650 rupiah on 707,000 shares, while the country's largest car maker Astra International rose 200 rupiah to 6,150 on 755,500 shares.
Brokers said the rise in Astra was linked to news that Astra would start exporting its popular minibus to ASEAN countries from 1998.

Rudyanto Hardjanto, president-director of Toyota Astra Motor, a unit of Astra International, was quoted by Bisnis Indonesia newspaper as saying between 2,500 and 3,000 units would be exported per month.

"The new minibus 'Kijang' car has a sexier and more prestigious look commpared to the boxy-looking current model. We believe it will secure Astra's future market share," Vickers Ballas Tamara said in its monthly report.
Small-cap transportation maintenance firm Centris rose 28.57 percent, or 400 rupiah, to 1,800 rupiah on 10.1 million shares on talk of possible acquisitions despite a company denial, brokers said.
Brokers also attributed the rise to expectations of higher 1996 revenue and a report that it had launched a 100-taxi service in Surabaya.

Paper maker Indah Kiat rose 75 rupiah to 1,800 rupiah on a volume of 3.6 million shares on continued expectations it would benefit from either stagnant or falling pulp prices following a sustained high level in the global pulp inventory, brokers said.
